comment_box: I am writing to express my opposition to the proposed regulation published on August 4, 2025 (RIN 2900-AS31), which aims to reinstate the exclusion of abortion services and counseling from the VA medical benefits package and CHAMPVA benefits package as specified in 38 CFR Part 17. This will lead to negatively impact women's health or even result in their deaths. In the first paragraph of the ACTION section, the regulation reinstates a complete exclusion that exceeds reasonable policy by removing coverage even in situations where a veteran's life or health is at risk or where the pregnancy resulted from rape or incest. I passionately encourage the VA to maintain at least the conditional exceptions set in 2022 to guarantee that veterans experiencing medical emergencies or trauma can access the care they require. In the second paragraph of the SUPPLEMENTARY INFORMATION section, the justification stems from the assertion that abortion services are not considered “needed” medical services under section 1710 of title 38; however, the term “needed” is not defined and should be interpreted through clinical judgment that is based on current medical standards, as care may be medically warranted in many specific situations. This exclusion will disproportionately affect veterans in rural regions or in states with higher restrictive abortion regulations, many of whom depend on the VA as their sole available medical provider. For this reason, the suggested language stating that “scope of coverage shall exclude abortion services and abortion counseling” should be amended to clearly permit exceptions where the attending VA healthcare provider considers the treatment medically necessary, especially when the veteran's life, health, or well-being is at risk, or in cases of rape or incest. Veterans who have served this country with honor deserve fair access to healthcare, and the proposed reinstatement does not align with the VA's mission of ensuring Veteran’s health and dignity. I respectfully urge the Department to rethink this stance of exclusion and maintain access to vital reproductive health services for veterans and their families.
